title: Klarna SUING People to collect their debt! (They want $130 million back!)
summary: A finance creator covers Klarna's lawsuits over unpaid debt, FICO's new BNPL credit scoring, and how the debt plays out in collections and bankruptcy.

assertions.quote: FICO, the main company behind credit scores, will begin including your buy now pay later payments in your credit score
This country has $1.2 trillion worth of outstanding credit card debt. And CLA, Afterpay, and all those guys just added to it

verdicts.note: Aggregate household debt data shows BNPL use growing alongside, not instead of, credit card balances.

assertions.quote: instead of you paying off your Afterpay, you then further put it on a credit card, meaning you're delaying the payment twice
not only do they actually buy it 40% more, we want 6% from you too, Mr. Retailer

verdicts.note: Higher average order values from BNPL checkout options and merchant discount fees are both well-documented parts of the BNPL business model.
NBER's 'Robin Hood effect': the merchant, not the consumer, pays for BNPL's zero-interest loan, funded by the sales and margin gains BNPL produces.

CFPB: BNPL lenders' data-driven targeting and product design confer financial benefits 'primarily through incremental merchant-discount-fee revenue and increased affiliate-fee and interchange revenue' -- fees paid by merchants, boosted by the spending increases BNPL produces.

assertions.quote: they can get you a 33 and a half%
A firm, CLA, Afterpay, all of those types of services, they are all dischargeable in a bankruptcy
At a certain point, if you're broke enough, you're so broke that you're this thing called judgment proof

verdicts.note: A real legal concept: with no attachable income or assets, a judgment can go unpaid for years, though wage garnishment still applies if the person later gets a job.

assertions.quote: if they can just keep increasing the limit that you'll take, they just keep giving you more and more rope to get yourself with

verdicts.note: A standard growth tactic once repayment history looks good, documented across unsecured lenders generally, BNPL included.
